evidence.quote: The male palm produces the pollen and the female palm produces the fruit.
evidence.doc: FAO Date Palm Cultivation (2002), Chapter VIII

pollination.notes: Fundamental species breeding system. The programme describes managed pollination; no fixed stocking ratio is prescribed for an unspecified farm.

supplementaryReferences.title: Kakamas phenology is not a picking calendar
supplementaryReferences.doc: FAO Date Palm Cultivation (2002), Chapter IV, Table 23
supplementaryReferences.note: Table is fruit-set-to-maturation duration, not months of ripe harvest. Its separate table lists July–August flowering. Neither becomes a food-availability bar.

supplementaryReferences.quote: In the southern hemisphere harvesting takes place in February, March and April.

supplementaryReferences.note: Broad hemispheric context, not a measured cultivar/site calendar. Kept outside the structured local harvest windows.

supplementaryReferences.title: Western Cape Medjool ripening and spoilage trial
supplementaryReferences.quote: irregular ripening and high incidences of microbial spoilage
supplementaryReferences.doc: Peddie (2023), Stellenbosch MScAgric thesis, university-provided abstract in FAO AGRIS
supplementaryReferences.note: 2022 trial at Kleinplasie near Hermon concerns Medjool. Abstract treatment dates label ripening stages inconsistently; no harvest months are inferred. Full university handle returned HTTP 403 during checking.

care: Female palms need suitable male pollen. Record sex, cultivar and pollination management before forecasting fruit.
Check heat, water and rain during ripening. The Hermon trial found uneven ripening and spoilage, so regional success alone does not establish a local crop.
purchase: Medjool is documented in the Hermon study. Obtain known fruiting female material and compatible pollen advice; a seedling's sex and eventual fruit quality are not established by its appearance.
